newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - April 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - April 8.

text.p: Following were the leading stories in Sri Lankan newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Japan offers three billion rupees in aid for drinking water project, says Public Utilities Minister Nimal Siripala de Silva.
Catholic Bishops Conference commends agreement between President Chandrika Kumaratunga and opposition leader Ranil Wickremesinghe to take a bipartisan approach to solve the ethnic conflict.

The ruling People's Alliance coalition will not take disciplinary action against constituent member Democratic United National (Lalith) Front (DUNF), political sources said. The DUNF was accused of backing independent candidates in last month's local government polls.

Engine oil worth over one million rupees, which was enroute to Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) separatists' camp in eastern Mullaitivu jungles, detected buried at a beach in in Uppuveli in Tirncomalee district, defence sources say.
Committee investigating crash of Kfir jet in January say cause was pilot error, according to defence sources.
Police to launch special security scheme to respond speedily to bank robberies and other crimes, says Police chief W.B. Rajaguru.
